newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse opens firmer, Dow, Bunds boost.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse opens firmer, Dow, Bunds boost.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse began stronger on Tuesday encouraged by a firmer Wall Street close and German Bund gains.
But trade was expected to be limited as the market holds back while Russian President Boris Yelsin undergoes a heart operation and the U.S. electorate go to the polls.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares was up 9.36 points, or 0.35 percent, at 2,681.22 by 1037 GMT.

Although Democrat U.S. President Bill Clinton is widely expected to win a second term, markets are watching to see whether the Republicans can hold onto their majority in the House of Representatives.
If the Democrats win a majority in the House, they are seen pursuing a less strict budget policy than the Republicans, which would worry markets.

The morning's biggest loser amongst the DAX stocks was Germany's largest bank Deutsche Bank. Traders said there had probably been a large sell order from a foreign investor and the fact the stock had dropped below the technical and psychological level of 70 marks was also weighing.
Deutsche fell 80 pfennigs, or over one percent, at 69.50 marks.
Meanwhile, German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG was slightly stronger than the market, rising 33 pfennigs to 57.33 marks, after the firm published nine-month results within expectations.

Shares in German pharmaceutical group Gehe were slightly up after the company announced a renewed takeover bid for UK firm Lloyds Chemists, offering 500 pence in cash per Lloyds share. Gehe added four marks to trade at 106 marks.
Gehe said it was confident its bid would be accepted.
